evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game can be implemented as a standalone capability without requiring another story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators ... access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators to access a game inherently depends on a game existing to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: start a round ... entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session context in which the round occurs.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing items for a session depends on items having been created/added for that session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that a list of items exists (items have been created/imported).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to a list for estimation presupposes an existing game/session context to hold that list.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item inherently depends on items already existing.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item inherently depends on items already existing.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates depends on an estimation round where estimates can be given.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates have been collected for a round/item.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on all estimators' cards depends on the mechanism for estimators to submit/show cards/estimates.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate depends on having an estimation context (item/round) and prior estimates/discussion.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating inherently depends on having previously estimated the story in the session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories implies there is a target game/session/list to import them into.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories implies there is a target game/session/list to add them to.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games can be implemented as a standalone feature over stored games; it does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on games existing (and having recorded stories/estimates) to view.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the existence of a transcript to export.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on the existence of a transcript to export.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently depends on games existing to delete.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a self-contained capability and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing to authenticate against.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display can be implemented independently as a formatting behavior wherever dates/times are shown; it does not inherently require another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders inherently depend on accounts (with email addresses) existing.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an estimation scale depends on having an estimation game/round where cards/estimates are used.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: This is an extension of inviting estimators and depends on the base invite capability and an existing game to invite to.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game via a received URL depends on the game being created and the URL/invitation being provided.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated depends on there being a game/round with an item selected/started.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items for the session depends on items existing for that session and being in a game the estimator has joined.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This depends on the ability for estimators to participate in a game and submit estimates.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after everyone has estimated depends on estimators being able to join and give estimates in a round.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of an estimation/draw mechanism where estimates are submitted and later revealed.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates depends on estimates having been recorded for that story in earlier rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Seeing who gave what depends on estimates being given/collected during a round.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer for participants presupposes a multiplayer game/session context with participants present.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the two-minute timer depends on the timer feature existing.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds depends on rounds having occurred and their stories/estimates being available.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering across draws depends on having a card/draw-based estimation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of a draw/estimation mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a participant photo near played cards depends on having participants in a game and a UI where cards are played.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting quality requirement that can be pursued independently of other specific stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary/list of definitions can be created as a standalone artifact/feature without requiring another story first.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is an internal optimization task that does not inherently depend on another specific backlog story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a general quality requirement and not inherently dependent on a particular other story.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a general quality requirement and not inherently dependent on another specific story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a general capability/constraint that can be implemented independently of other specific stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a general system behavior and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages can be implemented as a standalone cross-cutting feature without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results (even anonymized) presupposes that the application produces and stores results/estimates from games/rounds.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Usage metrics inherently depend on the game being used and events/data being generated by core gameplay features.
